newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek bourse poor 96 performer but cheapest play.
newsitem.headline: Greek bourse poor 96 performer but cheapest play.

text.p: The Athens stock exchange performed poorly in 1996, ranking 22nd out of 30 emerging markets in the IFC global index, but it has the lowest trading multiple and highest dividend yield, IFC said.

The International Finance Corporation (IFC) said the IFC global price index for Greece dropped 1.0 percent in dollar terms in 1996 compared to three-digit returns by other emerging markets like Russia and Venezuela.
"A number of positive and negative politico-economic events affected the Greek market during 1996," said IFC head market analyst Constantine Grigoriadis.

On the plus side, the most significant were the listing of state telecom OTE, the election of Costas Simitis as prime minister and improved macroeconomic figures -- falling inflation and interest rates.
But the share registration bill and the Delta Securities scandal were the low points.

Based on the latest IFC data for Greece's equities market -- the IFC investable index series -- the Athens bourse has the lowest market price earnings (P/E) ratio, x10.17, and the highest dividend yield, 6.28 percent, of all emerging markets, the IFC said.

"Further privatisation of state property, share dematerialisation and better trading and settlement systems are some of the measures foreign institutional investors expect to see in 1997," Grigoriadis said.
